summary: Intermittent head-of-line blocking from proxy write-serialization causing long tail inference latency and stream stalls
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed elevated p95/p99 generation latency and occasional streaming stalls for long-running completions (>30s). The pattern is intermittent across sessions and manifests as: initial tokens stream normally, then a ~10-30s pause with no bytes (stream silence), followed by either a connection reset or a burst of buffered tokens. Impact: customer-facing UX degradation (chat UI stalls), increased token cost due to retries, and some 504s for requests that exceed ALB idle window.

Impact:
- Affected customer: LumenDocs (dedicated cluster).
- Several production sessions across us-east and us-west.
- Observed p99 spike from ~1.2s -> 18-45s for some requests.

Environment and scope:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) behind our edge proxy and internal API gateway.
- TLS termination at ALB, downstream edge-proxy (envoy-based) maintaining upstream connections to serving runtime pods.
- Observed primarily on streaming generate endpoints with large trace headers and frequent auth token rotation.

Steps to reproduce (observed method):
1) Start a long generation with streaming enabled and a prompt that triggers a KV-cache warmup (context >2k tokens).
2) Simultaneously rotate client auth cookies every ~8s (customer-side telemetry) and enable verbose trace headers (x-trace-id, x-client-meta).
3) Observe the stream for 20-60s.

Observed behavior:
- Mid-stream silence (no bytes forwarded) for 10-30s, then resume with a burst of accumulated tokens or a TCP RST.
- Edge logs show upstream write attempts blocking on socket buffer flush (write throttled) during periods of header growth and small-chunk coalescing.
- ALB metrics show occasional ConnectionsClosedByClient coincident with proxy stalls.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous streaming with gradual token emission. Proxy should not block or coalesce writes in a way that starves warmup requests.

Immediate customer workaround suggested:
- Reduce client-side header churn (avoid rotating cookies while streaming) and disable verbose trace headers; use a stable x-trace for the session.
- If using dedicated routing, temporarily pin to a shorter sequence length or lower batch size to avoid prolonged KV warmup windows.

Attachments:
- Edge proxy logs (redacted) and packet capture slices attached in internal artifact store: s3://redwood-support/artifacts/SUP-52748/

investigation_notes: 2026-02-12 - Initial triage: dashboards show high WriteWait duration on edge-proxy instances serving the customer cluster (instance ids: ep-03, ep-07). Cumulative stalls line up with 5-15s gaps in streaming traces.

Packet capture (pcap) observation: TLS record sizes occasionally shrink to tiny frames when headers rotate; opposite burst when flush occurs. This pattern suggests write coalescing and delayed flush in the proxy (envoy) path.

Hypothesis v1: Frequent header updates cause the proxy to rewrite or reserialize HTTP/2 header frames and buffer data until HPACK table updates settle, leading to short-term head-of-line blocking for that stream.
Evidence: http2 debug logs show multiple CONTINUATION frames and HPACK table churn timed with silence windows.

Hypothesis v2: Underlying kernel/Nagle interactions on upstream socket combined with small TLS records cause the socket send buffer to be held until a coalescing threshold or timer triggers.
Evidence: socket sndbuf growth and tcp_info shows delayed ACK pacing during stall window.

Cross-checks: Other customers with low header churn and fewer small-chunk uploads are not impacted on same proxies. Replaying requests without header rotation reproduced the issue consistently at ~90% reproduction rate.
Metric links: Edge Proxy write_wait graph: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/d/proxy/write-wait?orgId=1&var-cluster=dedicated-lumendocs
Related runbooks: Edge proxy HPACK tuning and h2 stream management (internal).
root_cause: Combination of HTTP/2 header churn (frequent header/token rotation) and proxy write/coalescing behavior under small TLS record patterns caused transient write serialization. This produced head-of-line-like stalls for the affected stream, manifesting as mid-stream silence and occasional connection resets when upstream idle timers expired.
resolution:
Mitigation deployed: temporary config change on dedicated edge-proxy pool - reduce header coalescing timeout and enable immediate flush for streaming responses on paths matching /v1/generate-stream. Deployed to ep-03/ep-07. Customer advised to stabilize session tokens as short-term mitigation; confirmed reduction in incidents.
Permanent fix: upstream PR to envoy fork to adjust HTTP/2 HPACK table update handling and to bypass coalescing for streaming endpoints merged (https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/442). Rolling restart of proxy pool scheduled during low-traffic window (2026-02-20 02:00 UTC).
follow_up_tasks: Deploy proxy rolling restart to remaining dedicated pools (2026-02-20) and monitor write_wait and p99 latency for streaming endpoints.
Add a telemetry alert to flag incremental HPACK churn per-connection > 50 updates/min and correlate with write_wait spikes.
Update customer-facing KB: guidance on session token rotation best practices for streaming (add to support knowledge base).
Add integration test to the edge-proxy test harness that replays header-rotation scenarios and asserts no streaming stalls >3s.
Postmortem: draft postmortem page linking artifacts and root cause analysis (owner: Marcus Reed, due 2026-02-25).
